items.title: A weakness has been identified in Tenstorrent tt-metal up to 0.80.0. The affected element is the...
items.summary: A weakness has been identified in Tenstorrent tt-metal up to 0.80.0. The affected element is the function load_hf_state_dict_filtered of the file models/tt_transformers/tt/load_checkpoints.py. This manipulation of the argument weight_map causes path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 0.81.0-dev20261016 is sufficient to fix this issue. Patch name: 4851ccf347f6903c3d819eed60705600386e52c3. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

items.title: The Duplicator and Duplicator Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in...
items.summary: The Duplicator and Duplicator Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.17 and 4.6.10, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted database content in DUPX_UpdateEngine::unserializeTest() during migration. This allows unauthenticated attackers to store a serialized object in public site content before an administrator builds a package and later performs a migration or import that runs database search-and-replace. Duplicator Free bundles a Requests 1.7 POP chain that permits attacker-selected callbacks, resulting in direct operating-system command execution. Duplicator Pro bundles an IndexList destructor gadget that permits deletion of an attacker-selected existing file when its containing directory is writable by the installer PHP process; deletion of wp-config.php can expose the setup wizard and lead to site takeover and code execution if the attacker reaches it first and supplies a reachable database they control. The package must be created after the carrier is stored, and a later administrator migration action is required.

items.summary: A security vulnerability has been detected in Tenda AC19 16.03.10.07. The impacted element is the function formSetFirewallCfg of the file /goform/SetFirewallCfg of the component httpd Web Management Service. Such manipulation of the argument firewallEn leads to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

items.title: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contains an optimizer miscompilation in which (msg.value | K) or (len...
items.summary: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contains an optimizer miscompilation in which (msg.value | K) or (len(msg.data) | K), where K is any nonzero integer literal, is compiled to the constant 1 when used as a ternary expression branch under -O gas (the default) or -O codesize. Affected contracts use the wrong value in storage writes, arithmetic, indexes, return values, or events without warning or revert, which can record deposits incorrectly and lock funds.

items.title: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b12, 0.1.0b14, and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 mix character-based line...
items.summary: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b12, 0.1.0b14, and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 mix character-based line offsets with Python's UTF-8 byte col_offset values in vyper/ast/parse.py, so multi-byte characters shift the source slices used to reconstruct later numeric literals. An attacker contributing source with non-ASCII identifiers that NFKC-normalize to ASCII, or an invisible byte-order mark, can silently substitute addresses, integers or other constants in compiled code.

items.title: Vyper 0.3.4 through 0.5.0b1 computes the remaining blueprint size in create_from_blueprint by...
items.summary: Vyper 0.3.4 through 0.5.0b1 computes the remaining blueprint size in create_from_blueprint by uint256 subtraction without first checking that code_offset is below the blueprint's code size, so a huge offset wraps to a small positive value. An attacker controlling code_offset can make a factory deploy contracts with no runtime code, potentially trapping ETH and tokens.

items.title: Best Practice Software Bp Premier before 1.14.1.1128 uses a hardcoded Microsoft SQL Server...
items.summary: Best Practice Software Bp Premier before 1.14.1.1128 uses a hardcoded Microsoft SQL Server administrative password that is shared across all installations and cannot be changed without breaking the application. Attackers with network access to the database instance can authenticate as sysadmin, bypass application authentication, and execute operating system commands as SYSTEM.

items.title: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contains a compiler miscompilation vulnerability in parse_IfExp that...
items.summary: Vyper 0.3.8 through 0.5.0b1 contains a compiler miscompilation vulnerability in parse_IfExp that reads nested arrays with narrower inner bounds using the wider result type's memory layout. When a ternary selects the narrower array, inner arrays after the first are read at wrong offsets, causing contracts to silently store corrupted values or revert.

items.title: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b17 and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 builds its source-line table with str...
items.summary: Vyper 0.1.0b1 before 0.1.0b17 and 0.4.1 through 0.5.0b1 builds its source-line table with str.splitlines(), which treats characters like form feed and U+2028 as line breaks the Python parser ignores, so numeric literals are classified and validated from shifted source text. An attacker contributing source code can hide these characters in comments, strings or indentation to silently change address, integer or decimal constants.

items.title: uv before 0.11.15 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious wheels to write...
items.summary: uv before 0.11.15 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious wheels to write files outside the scripts directory via crafted console_scripts or gui_scripts entry point names. Attackers who induce users to install a malicious wheel can place executables in PATH directories, shadowing or overwriting existing binaries for code execution.

items.title: Astral uv before 0.11.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to delete...
items.summary: Astral uv before 0.11.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows attackers to delete arbitrary files by supplying wheels with relative traversal paths in RECORD entries. Attackers can craft a malicious wheel whose RECORD references files outside the installation prefix, causing uv to delete those files when the user uninstalls the package.

items.title: sharp before 0.35.5 bundles a librsvg dependency affected by a memory-related vulnerability (CVE...
items.summary: sharp before 0.35.5 bundles a librsvg dependency affected by a memory-related vulnerability (CVE-2026-96889) that, under certain runtime-specific conditions, can lead to code execution on glibc-based Linux. An attacker can supply a crafted SVG image that, when decoded by sharp through librsvg, may result in arbitrary code execution.

items.title: Sharp before 0.35.4 bundles a vulnerable libheif dependency that allows attackers to achieve...
items.summary: Sharp before 0.35.4 bundles a vulnerable libheif dependency that allows attackers to achieve possible remote code execution on glibc-based Linux by supplying crafted images. Attackers can submit malicious AVIF/HEIF input to applications processing untrusted images with sharp, triggering libheif decoding flaws to execute code.

items.title: Sharp before 0.35.0 bundles a version of libvips affected by multiple vulnerabilities (CVE-2026...
items.summary: Sharp before 0.35.0 bundles a version of libvips affected by multiple vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-33327, CVE-2026-33328, CVE-2026-35590, CVE-2026-35591 and CVE-2026-69242) in its GIF, TIFF and VIPS image decoders. Attackers can supply crafted GIF, TIFF or VIPS files to applications using sharp to process untrusted input, triggering these libvips flaws.

items.title: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that...
items.summary: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access the FastAPI surface because require_auth() returns early when API_AUTH_KEY is unset. Attackers can post messages to /sessions/{id}/messages to trigger root shell commands via BashTool, upload .py or .sh files via /upload, read session histories, and obtain partial API keys.

items.title: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains an indirect prompt injection vulnerability...
items.summary: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains an indirect prompt injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute shell commands as root by planting instructions in documents or web pages the agent processes. BashTool and BackgroundRunTool pass model-emitted commands to subprocess.run with shell=True and no allow-list or approval step, and read_url fetches arbitrary URLs, enabling command execution and server-side request forgery.

items.title: adm-zip 0.6.0 contains a decompression bomb protection bypass that allows attackers to evade the...
items.summary: adm-zip 0.6.0 contains a decompression bomb protection bypass that allows attackers to evade the maxOutputLength guard by targeting the asynchronous getDataAsync() path in methods/inflater.js. Attackers can craft ZIP entries with falsified small declared sizes and high-ratio DEFLATE payloads to exhaust memory in applications reading entries asynchronously.

items.title: Coraza from 3.0.0 before 3.8.1 has a JSON body processor that flattens nested properties into dot...
items.summary: Coraza from 3.0.0 before 3.8.1 has a JSON body processor that flattens nested properties into dot-separated ARGS_POST names without escaping literal dots, so distinct properties collide. Unauthenticated attackers can add a later dotted property such as account.role that overwrites a malicious nested value, hiding SQL injection payloads from OWASP CRS rules while backends still receive them.

items.title: Dulwich before 1.2.9 contains a denial of service vulnerability in Pack.resolve_object that...
items.summary: Dulwich before 1.2.9 contains a denial of service vulnerability in Pack.resolve_object that allows attackers to cause infinite recursion via self-referential OFS_DELTA objects. Attackers can supply a malicious packfile with an OFS_DELTA delta_offset of 0 to exhaust CPU during clone, fetch, or cat-file operations.

items.title: Dulwich from 0.22.5 before 1.2.8 contains a path traversal vulnerability in stash.py pop() that...
items.summary: Dulwich from 0.22.5 before 1.2.8 contains a path traversal vulnerability in stash.py pop() that allows attackers to write arbitrary files outside the worktree through intermediate directory symlinks. Attackers can craft a malicious repository whose popped stash writes a payload into .git/hooks/post-checkout, achieving code execution on the next checkout.

items.title: adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains an inconsistent entry resolution vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains an inconsistent entry resolution vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass content validation by supplying ZIP archives with duplicate entry names. Attackers can craft archives where getEntry() returns the last duplicate while extractAllTo() writes the first, causing unvalidated bytes to be written to disk.

items.title: adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated...
items.summary: adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the Node.js process via a malformed ZIP file, because inflateAsync in methods/inflater.js lacks a zlib stream error listener. Attackers can supply a ZIP with corrupted DEFLATE data processed by readFileAsync, readAsTextAsync, extractAllToAsync, or getDataAsync, triggering an uncatchable exception that terminates all in-flight requests.

items.title: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: HKUDS Vibe-Trading from 0.1.0 before 0.1.7 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows remote attackers to read sensitive server files through LLM agent file-read tools. Attackers can prompt the agent to invoke read_document, which lacks sandbox checks, or safe_user_path-gated tools to leak /etc/shadow, /proc/self/environ API keys, and /root credentials.

items.title: Dulwich from 0.24.0 before 1.2.8 contains a symlink following vulnerability in porcelain.checkout...
items.summary: Dulwich from 0.24.0 before 1.2.8 contains a symlink following vulnerability in porcelain.checkout(paths=[...]) that allows attackers to write arbitrary files by abusing raw os.open without O_NOFOLLOW. Attackers can craft a repository where a worktree symlink points to .git/hooks/post-checkout, so restoring the file from a tag writes a malicious hook for code execution.

items.title: Coraza before 3.8.1 extracts multipart upload filenames with Go's mime.ParseMediaType, which...
items.summary: Coraza before 3.8.1 extracts multipart upload filenames with Go's mime.ParseMediaType, which silently ignores RFC 5987 filename* parameters whose charset is not utf-8 or us-ascii. Unauthenticated attackers can send a decoy filename with filename*=iso-8859-1''shell.php, or filename* alone, so FILES-based rules never see the real name, letting dangerous uploads reach backends that honor filename*.

items.title: Adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: Adm-zip before 0.6.1 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that allows attackers to set setuid, setgid, or sticky bits on extracted files when keepOriginalPermission is enabled. Attackers can craft zip external file attributes that pass unmasked into chmod, letting attacker-controlled executables gain elevated privileges when extracted as root and later run.

items.summary: Coraza from 3.0.4 before 3.8.1 contains a request body inspection bypass because request-body processor selection compares the entire Content-Type value exactly, so URL-encoded bodies whose Content-Type carries a media-type parameter are never parsed. Unauthenticated attackers can send application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8 to keep ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY empty, evading body rules while the backend still processes the payload.

items.summary: Dulwich from 0.23.1 before 1.2.8 contains a path traversal vulnerability in CommitFilter._apply_index_filter() that allows attackers to write files outside the working directory via symlinks persisting between commits. Attackers can craft a repository where an ancestor commit's symlink redirects a descendant commit's file writes during filter_branch, enabling code execution by writing into .git/hooks.

items.title: Dulwich before 1.2.9 fails to validate DOS drive letter prefixes in Git tree path elements on...
items.summary: Dulwich before 1.2.9 fails to validate DOS drive letter prefixes in Git tree path elements on Windows, allowing arbitrary file write. Attackers can craft a malicious repository with a tree entry named 'C:' that bypasses NTFS validation and writes files outside the worktree to achieve remote code execution.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to log out authenticated users by sending a link to the GET-based /logout endpoint. items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0 looks up runs by friendlyId alone in the api.v1.runs.$runParam.replay route without scoping the lookup to the caller's runtime environment. An attacker holding any tenant's API key who knows a victim's run friendlyId can replay that run into their own environment and read the victim's task payload.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.0 performs no authentication or organization check in the action handler of the dashboard run replay route (resources.taskruns.$runParam.replay) and looks up the run by friendlyId alone. A remote attacker who knows a victim's run friendlyId can replay it into an environment of their choosing, exposing the victim's task payload or running the task again with the victim's secrets.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the CLI...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the CLI authorization-code flow because loading /account/authorization-code/<code> mints a Personal Access Token without any consent step. Attackers mint an unauthenticated code, lure a logged-in user to that URL, then retrieve the victim's PAT from the unauthenticated /api/v1/token endpoint to take over the account.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 self-hosted Docker Compose deployments using the default secrets from hosting/docker/.env.example allow authentication bypass because the hardcoded MAGIC_LINK_SECRET lets anyone forge valid magic link tokens. Unauthenticated attackers can log in as any email address, then reach Postgres, Redis, and ClickHouse with default credentials from runner containers on infrastructure networks, compromising all tenant data.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.5.4 contains a hardcoded default secret vulnerability in the /coordinator...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.4 contains a hardcoded default secret vulnerability in the /coordinator Socket.IO namespace that allows unauthenticated attackers to connect using the published coordinator-secret value. Attackers can emit READY_FOR_EXECUTION to retrieve decrypted run environment variables or send TASK_RUN_FAILED_TO_RUN and similar events to tamper with arbitrary runs.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the TSQL query compiler, which concatenates window-function names into generated ClickHouse SQL without allowlisting or escaping. Authenticated customers can submit a backtick-quoted identifier to POST /api/v1/query that injects a raw subquery outside the per-tenant WHERE guard, exfiltrating other organizations' analytics data.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.6.2 contains an authorization vulnerability that allows public-token holders with session write access to obtain environment-wide S2 stream credentials via session input initialization. Attackers can use the credential directly against the storage API to append, create, or trim other session and run streams, forging output or permanently deleting records.

Attackers holding one valid API key can supply ../ sequences to obtain presigned GET or PUT URLs and read or overwrite other tenants' run payloads and outputs.

items.summary: Trigger.dev through 4.7.6 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the supervisor workload server that allows workloads to manipulate runs belonging to other deployments without ownership verification. Attackers with network access and a valid run/snapshot pair can call the attempts/start endpoint to obtain resolved environment variables and run JWTs, or start, complete, and suspend other tenants' runs.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in DeleteTaskScheduleService and SetActiveOnTaskScheduleService that allows authenticated users to delete or disable other organizations' schedules. Attackers can send delete or disable actions through their own project's schedule route with a victim schedule friendlyId to destroy other organizations' IMPERATIVE cron schedules.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to make the server send requests by setting unvalidated alert-channel webhook URLs. items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows holders of lower-trust environment API keys to cancel other environments' deployments because DeploymentService.getDeployment scopes lookups by projectId only. items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the /realtime/v1/runs endpoint, which concatenates the unescaped tags query parameter into the ElectricSQL shape where clause and defeats the runtimeEnvironmentId tenant guard. Authenticated attackers holding any project API key with read:runs scope can append boolean conditions to stream TaskRun records, including payloads and metadata, from every organization on the same self-hosted instance.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in createDeploymentBackgroundWorkerV4 that resolves a WorkerDeployment by friendlyId alone, without environment, project, or organization scoping. Attackers holding only their own environment API key can POST to the deployment background-workers endpoint with a victim's deployment ID to re-point that in-progress deployment at a worker in the attacker's environment.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows holders of capability-restricted user-actor tokens to create alert channels by using the legacy personal access token helper. Attackers with a read-only UAT can POST to the project alertChannels endpoint to create production webhook channels, routing future deployment and error alerts to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

items.summary: The Trigger.dev webapp before 4.5.12 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in its organization-level Slack OAuth flow, which uses the organization ID as the OAuth state without binding it to the initiating session. Attackers who know a target organization ID can trick an authenticated member into opening an unredeemed /integrations/slack/callback URL, connecting an attacker-controlled Slack workspace that may receive the organization's operational alerts.

items.title: Trigger.dev CLI before 4.5.9 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that exposes...
items.summary: Trigger.dev CLI before 4.5.9 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that exposes resolved environment secret values in debug deployment logs by serializing unredacted envVars. items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.2 contains a blind server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated tenants to make the webapp server send POST requests to internal hosts by setting an unvalidated webhook alert channel URL. items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.10 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to bypass webhook SSRF protections by targeting the non-global 198.18.0.0/15 benchmarking range. Attackers can configure alert-channel webhooks pointing at internally routed services in this range, which isUnsafeIPv4 omits, to perform blind internal probing and limited state-changing POST requests.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.6.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the GET /api/v1/projects/:projectRef/envvars endpoint, which returns the environment's root API key as TRIGGER_SECRET_KEY for staging, production, and preview environments. Attackers holding a restricted read:envvars key can obtain the root secret and plaintext secrets, then trigger tasks and mint admin public JWTs.

items.summary: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the Dashboard Agent input proxy that stores a delegated user-actor token in browser-readable session input records. Attackers holding a chat's public session token can read the in records endpoint to recover the token from payload.metadata.userActorToken and replay it for environment JWT exchange.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.5.12 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to complete another member's DEVELOPMENT environment waitpoint by skipping the per-user environment ownership check. Attackers who know a victim's waitpoint friendly ID can submit type=DATETIME or type=MANUAL with isTimeout to prematurely mark the pending waitpoint completed.

items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.6.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the waitpoint token wait endpoint that allows authenticated attackers to block runs belonging to other organizations. Attackers holding any secret API key can supply a victim run ID with their own waitpoint, causing that run to block indefinitely on a waitpoint the victim cannot complete, and can inject resume data into it.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.7.3 contains a tenant filtering bypass vulnerability that allows...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.7.3 contains a tenant filtering bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read other tenants' data by using placeholder table syntax in POST /api/v1/query. Attackers can submit queries with FROM {database.table} expressions, including within subqueries, to skip table allowlist and tenant filters and expose run metadata and payloads.

items.title: Snipe-IT before 8.7.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the webhook testing...
items.summary: Snipe-IT before 8.7.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the webhook testing feature that allows super-admin users to probe internal network addresses, including loopback and RFC1918 ranges. Attackers can point webhooks at internal hosts and ports, then compare 4xx versus 5xx responses from Test Webhooks to map open ports and active hosts.

items.title: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the PUT...
items.summary: Trigger.dev 4.5.0 before 4.6.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the PUT snapshot-url session endpoint that allows public session token holders to obtain presigned S3 write URLs. End users can overwrite their own session's durable chat snapshot to forge the agent's conversation history, since the route lacks a secret-key-only check.

items.title: Trigger.dev before 4.7.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows holders of...
items.summary: Trigger.dev before 4.7.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows holders of unrestricted environment API keys to block runs they do not own by supplying a foreign parentRunId to batch-creation endpoints. Attackers can send requests to POST /api/v3/batches or POST /api/v2/tasks/batch with resumeParentOnCompletion to suspend, indefinitely block, or inject errors into production or cross-organization runs.

items.summary: SvelteKit before 3.0.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to reach internal services because self-fetch fallbacks follow HTTP redirects automatically. Attackers can manipulate the Host or forwarded headers to point fallback requests at their server, which redirects them to internal services.

items.summary: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) before 3.0.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability in enhanced form actions (use:enhance) on routes accepting paths beginning with a double slash. Attackers can craft action paths starting with // that become protocol-relative URLs, causing non-redirect form results to navigate victims to attacker-controlled sites.

items.title: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) from 2.10.0 before 3.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the...
items.summary: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) from 2.10.0 before 3.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the vite preview server on Windows that allows unauthenticated attackers to read files outside the prerendered output directory. Attackers who can reach the preview server through network access or a tunnel can send crafted requests to expose source code, configuration, or credentials readable by the server process.

items.title: SvelteKit (@sveltejs/kit) before 3.0.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in...

items.title: A2A Java SDK: Push notification credentials logged in cleartext on protobuf parse failure
items.summary:
### *Impact.** Push notification bearer tokens and authentication credentials submitted by clients are written to server log files in cleartext. Any operator, log aggregation system, or attacker with log access can read these secrets and use them to authenticate to the client's push notification endpoints, potentially sending forged task status updates.

**Where.** `transport/rest/src/main/java/org/a2aproject/sdk/transport/rest/handler/RestHandler.java:676` in `parseRequestBody`

**What.** The `parseRequestBody` method logs the entire JSON request body at `SEVERE` level when `JsonFormat.parser().merge()` throws `InvalidProtocolBufferException`. This method is called from `createTaskPushNotificationConfiguration` (line 377), where the body contains client-supplied push notification bearer tokens (field `token`) and authentication credentials (field `authentication.credentials`). These secrets are written to server log files in full.

**Exploit scenario.** A client creates a push notification configuration by POSTing to `/v1/tenants/{tenant}/tasks/{taskId}/pushNotificationConfigs` with a body containing `{"url": "https://client.example.com/webhook", "token": "secret-bearer-token", "authentication": {"scheme": "Bearer", "credentials": "oauth-access-token"}, "extraField": "value"}`. The extra field causes `JsonFormat.parser().merge()` to throw `InvalidProtocolBufferException`. The entire body including `secret-bearer-token` and `oauth-access-token` is logged at SEVERE level. An attacker with log access retrieves the cleartext credentials.

**Preconditions.**
- Attacker must have access to server log files (centralized logging, log aggregation, shared infrastructure, or insider access)
- Push notification capability must be enabled
- A request body must fail protobuf deserialization while being valid JSON (unknown fields with strict parsing, schema mismatches)

**Fix.** Do not log the raw request body. Log only a sanitized summary — body length and content type, not content. Replace the log call with something like: `log.log(Level.SEVERE, "Error parsing JSON request body (length={0})", body != null ? body.length() : 0)`.

**Verification.** 3/3 lens verifiers confirmed.

items.title: A2A Java SDK: Android synchronous POST forwards credentials across authorities after incomplete redirect fix
items.summary:
The GHSA-9rhm fix added this safe setting in
AndroidA2AHttpClient.createConnection():

    connection.setInstanceFollowRedirects(false);

The synchronous POST builder later overwrites it:

    private boolean followRedirects = true;

    public A2AHttpResponse post() throws IOException {
        HttpURLConnection connection = createConnection("POST", false);
        connection.setInstanceFollowRedirects(followRedirects);
        // ...
    }

The second assignment wins. JSONRPCTransport and RestTransport both
add interceptor-produced headers and call synchronous post() without
setting followRedirects(false).

On Android's repackaged OkHttp implementation, a cross-authority
redirect strips Authorization but retains nonstandard request headers.
AuthInterceptor permits four nonstandard authentication header names:

    X-API-Key
    API-Key
    X-Auth-Token
    X-Authentication

I confirmed that the exact v1.3.1.Final Maven artifact forwards
complete synthetic values under all four names to a second loopback
authority. I also reproduced the supported AuthInterceptor to Android
POST path. Explicitly calling followRedirects(false) returns the
original 302 and produces no request to the collector.

All test traffic stayed on two ephemeral 127.0.0.1 listeners. All
credentials were synthetic FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-* values.

Reproduction

I have attached AndroidA2AHttpClientRedirectTest.java. Copy it to:

    extras/http-client-android/src/test/java/org/a2aproject/sdk/client/http/android/

Run:

    mvn -pl extras/http-client-android -am \
      -Dtest=AndroidA2AHttpClientRedirectTest \
      -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test

On unpatched current main, the default test fails with:

    Android synchronous POST must retain the documented no-redirect default
    expected: <302> but was: <200>

The explicit followRedirects(true) control still passes.

The separate exact-artifact fixture passed three consecutive runs. Its
relevant output was:

    default status=200 x-api-key=FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-DIRECT
authorization=null method=GET
    control-followRedirects-false status=302 collectorHits=0
    interceptor-chain status=200
x-api-key=FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-INTERCEPTOR collectorHits=1
    header-matrix name=X-API-Key forwarded=FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-X-API-Key
    header-matrix name=API-Key forwarded=FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-API-Key
    header-matrix name=X-Auth-Token forwarded=FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-X-Auth-Token
    header-matrix name=X-Authentication
forwarded=FULCRUM-SYNTHETIC-X-Authentication

Impact and limitations

The demonstrated impact is disclosure of a complete API key or
authentication token to a different authority. I am not claiming
subsequent use of the credential, integrity impact, availability
impact, code execution, or host compromise.

A fully malicious origin already receives the credential on the first
request. The additional boundary matters most when redirect or
front-door behavior is compromised separately from the component that
handles request credentials, or when different parts of the origin
operate in different trust domains.

The 7.5 score applies to an autonomous client where no human action is

items.title: A2A Java SDK has Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in push-notification delivery
items.summary:
---

- **Ecosystem:** Maven
- **Affected package:** `org.a2aproject.sdk:a2a-java-sdk-server-common` (push-notification delivery)
- **Affected versions:** `<= 1.2.0.Final` (and `1.2.1.Final-SNAPSHOT` on `main` prior to the fix)
- **Patched version:** _(the release that carries the fix)_
- **CWE:** CWE-918 (Server-Side Request Forgery)
- **Severity:** High
- **CVSS v3.1:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N` (5.8, Moderate)

---

## Summary

An **unauthenticated** attacker can coerce the a2a-java server into issuing HTTP requests to
arbitrary internal and cloud-metadata endpoints from the server's own network position — a
Server-Side Request Forgery reachable in the default deployment with no credentials, no user
interaction, and a single request. The behaviour is the shipped default, not a misconfiguration.

## Details

`BasePushNotificationSender` (in `server-common`) POSTs task data to the URL stored on a task's
`TaskPushNotificationConfig` with no validation of the destination: no block on loopback, RFC1918,
link-local (`169.254.0.0/16`, including the `169.254.169.254` metadata address), unique-local,
unspecified, or multicast ranges; no scheme restriction; and no bound on redirects.
`InMemoryPushNotificationConfigStore.setInfo` stores the URL verbatim and
`onCreateTaskPushNotificationConfig` does not check it either.

Both shipped HTTP clients follow redirects (`JdkA2AHttpClient` → `followRedirects(NORMAL)`,
`VertxA2AHttpClient` → `setFollowRedirects(true)`), so a creation-time URL allowlist is bypassable:
an attacker webhook answers `302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/...` and the client follows it. A
hostname check is likewise defeated by DNS rebinding. A correct guard must validate the *resolved*
IP of every hop at connection time, not the URL string.

## Exploitation

Demonstrated end-to-end against a running server (default wiring, unauthenticated caller):

- **Arbitrary internal reachability.** The attacker picks the destination and the server issues
  the request from inside the trust boundary. Delivery to loopback and to a real RFC1918 LAN
  address was exercised at runtime; because the code applies no destination filtering of any kind,
  the same path reaches link-local / metadata (`169.254.169.254`) and other internal ranges
  wherever network routing permits.
- **Allowlist + method bypass via redirect.** A `302` from the attacker's webhook reaches
  destinations a creation-time allowlist would block, and a `302` on a `POST` is followed as a
  `GET` — so GET-only endpoints such as the IMDS credentials path are reachable even though the
  sender only issues `POST`s. This is why a URL allowlist is not a sufficient fix; the guard must
  validate the resolved IP of every redirect hop.
- **Data push into internal services.** On direct (non-redirected) delivery, each request carries
  the task payload in the body, so internal services that ingest POST data receive
  attacker-influenced content (basis for `I:L`). On a redirected request the body is dropped in the
  POST→GET conversion, so the body-push and the redirect-reach are separate capabilities, not
  simultaneous on one request.

The sender discards the fetched response and exposes no caller-visible difference between a
successful and a failed delivery (both paths return without surfacing status or body), so the base
case reads back nothing — confidentiality is scored `C:N`. Read-back is limited, reach is not: the
attacker still drives fully controlled requests to metadata and internal services and writes data
into them.

1. Start a local listener standing in for an internal target (no real metadata service is touched).

items.title: A2A Java SDK has a fail-open default task authorization
items.summary:
Draft text for GHSA-qw47-mcm5-934w. The body below drops into the GitHub advisory description
field; the metadata block maps to the form fields. Set the patched version at release; publish
when the fix ships._

---

- **Ecosystem:** Maven
- **Affected package:** `org.a2aproject.sdk:a2a-java-sdk-server-common` (task store / authorization)
- **Affected versions:** `<= 1.2.0.Final` (and `1.2.1.Final-SNAPSHOT` on `main` prior to the fix)
- **Patched version:** _(the release that carries the fix, e.g. 1.2.1.Final)_
- **CWE:** CWE-1188 (Insecure Default Initialization), CWE-862 (Missing Authorization)
- **Severity:** High
- **CVSS v3.1:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` (7.5, High)

---

## Details

The default task store performs no authorization on task reads. `InMemoryTaskStore`'s no-arg
constructor sets `authorizationProvider = null`, and `InMemoryTaskStore.get(String taskId)` is a
bare map lookup with no authorization check regardless of provider:

```java
public InMemoryTaskStore() {
    this.authorizationProvider = null;   // default wiring
}

@Override
public @Nullable Task get(String taskId) {
    return tasks.get(taskId);            // no owner / caller check
}
```

Authorization is enforced only when the application both supplies a `TaskAuthorizationProvider`
*and* routes requests through `AuthorizationRequestHandlerDecorator` (via CDI), which checks
ownership before delegating. A server that uses the default store, or wires
`DefaultRequestHandler.builder().build()` manually, or integrates through a non-CDI stack (e.g.
Spring), never reaches that check. The safe posture is therefore opt-in and the shipped default is
the unsafe one. A caller can read a task created by another caller simply by knowing or guessing
its id.

## Summary

With the SDK's default configuration, task reads are not authorized: any caller can retrieve a
task (including its status, context, message history, and artifacts) created by another caller,
by supplying the task id.

## PoC

Using only the real production classes wired the default way (no mocks):

1. Construct the default store: `InMemoryTaskStore store = new InMemoryTaskStore();` (no-arg
   constructor, so no authorization provider).
2. As one caller, save a task: `store.save(victimTask, false);` with id `victim-task-42`.

items.title: A2A Java SDK send client credentials under server-controlled HTTP header name, enabling leakage via redirect
items.summary:
*Impact.** A malicious or compromised A2A agent can cause the client's API key credential to be forwarded to an arbitrary third-party server. The agent serves an AgentCard with an `APIKeySecurityScheme` specifying a custom header name, then responds with an HTTP redirect. The JDK HttpClient follows the redirect and forwards the custom header containing the credential, since only the standard `Authorization` header may be stripped on cross-origin redirects.

**Where.** `client/transport/spi/src/main/java/org/a2aproject/sdk/client/transport/spi/interceptors/auth/AuthInterceptor.java:69` in `intercept`

**What.** The `apiKeySecurityScheme.name()` field from the remote agent's AgentCard (untrusted, server-controlled data) is used directly as the HTTP header name when placing client credentials. Combined with `JdkA2AHttpClient`'s `followRedirects(NORMAL)` policy, credentials under custom header names survive cross-origin redirects (only `Authorization` is stripped on newer JDKs), allowing a malicious agent to leak client credentials to third-party servers. Additionally, `AuthInterceptor` does not check that `location==HEADER` before placing the credential as a header.

**Exploit scenario.** Client configures an API key credential for agent's security scheme `myAuth`. The malicious agent returns an AgentCard where `securitySchemes` includes `myAuth` as `APIKeySecurityScheme` with `name='X-Leaked-Cred'` and `location=HEADER`. `AuthInterceptor` places the credential in the `X-Leaked-Cred` header. The agent responds with HTTP 302 redirect to `https://evil.com/collect`. `JdkA2AHttpClient` follows the redirect, forwarding all custom headers including `X-Leaked-Cred` to `evil.com`. The attacker captures the client's credential.

**Preconditions.**
- Client application has configured API key credentials via `CredentialService` for the agent's security scheme
- The agent is malicious or compromised (controls its own AgentCard response)
- The default `JdkA2AHttpClient` is used (with `followRedirects=NORMAL`)
- The JDK version does not strip custom headers on cross-origin redirects (all current versions)

**Fix.** Validate the `APIKeySecurityScheme.name()` field against a whitelist of safe header names. Check that `apiKeySecurityScheme.location()` equals `Location.HEADER` before placing the credential as a header. Consider using `followRedirects(NEVER)` and implementing manual redirect handling that strips all authentication headers on cross-origin redirects.

**Verification.** 2/3 lens verifiers confirmed.

items.title: Pillow: Out-of-bounds access in _imagingmorph on a zero-width image
items.summary:
### Summary
A PPM or PGM file can declare a width of 0, which Pillow accepts, producing an image of size `(0, N)`. Passing that image to `ImageMorph.MorphOp.apply()` makes the native morphology code index a row buffer at `outrow[width - 1]`, which is `outrow[-1]` when the width is 0. The process crashes.

### Details
The PPM parser reads width and height with no lower-bound check:

- `src/PIL/PpmImagePlugin.py:119`

The native `apply()` writes the row edges with no guard that the width is positive:

- `src/_imagingmorph.c:81` sets `outrow[0] = outrow[width - 1] = 0;`

`match()` and `get_on_pixels()` use the same edge-indexing pattern.

### PoC
```python
from PIL import Image, ImageMorph

# A width-0 image (also producible from a crafted PPM header). apply() indexes
# outrow[width - 1] == outrow[-1] in native code.
im = Image.new("L", (0, 5))
ImageMorph.MorphOp(op_name="dilation4").apply(im)
```

Run it:
```
$ python 03_poc.py
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Observed on a source build of commit `3e2ab96`.

Under AddressSanitizer:
```
==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address (pc ... in apply)
    #0 apply   src/_imagingmorph.c:81
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV src/_imagingmorph.c:81 in apply
```
With width 0 the `outrow[width - 1]` write lands on an unmapped page, so it surfaces as a SEGV pinned to the edge-write line rather than a redzone overflow.

### Impact
Out-of-bounds write in a C extension. Affects any application that runs a morphology operation on an image opened from untrusted input. Result is a crash and possible memory corruption.

items.title: Pillow: GIF seek keeps rejected size after DecompressionBombError, allowing DoS
items.summary:
```
============================================================================
GIF seek keeps rejected size after DecompressionBombError, allowing DoS
Location: src/PIL/GifImagePlugin.py:293  in GifImageFile._seek()
Commit:   a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6
============================================================================
```

A GIF of about 60 bytes can make Pillow allocate gigabytes of memory. This affects applications that catch the "image too large" error raised while stepping to a later animation frame and then keep using the same image object. Pillow correctly refuses the oversized frame, but it stores the refused dimensions on the image object anyway, and later operations size their memory from them. An attacker who can upload a GIF to such a service can exhaust its memory: the process either fails with an out-of-memory error after committing gigabytes, or is killed by the operating system. There is no memory corruption.

The bug is in `GifImageFile._seek()` (`src/PIL/GifImagePlugin.py:292-294`). When a frame's extent enlarges the image, the code assigns the new size to `self._size` and only then calls `Image._decompression_bomb_check()`. Nothing restores the old size when `DecompressionBombError` is raised, because `seek()` only rolls back on `EOFError`. After the caught error, `im.size` reports the rejected size while the pixel buffer `im.im` is still the 1×1 first frame. Because the extent is a 16-bit offset plus a 16-bit size, that rejected size can be as large as 131070×131070.

In the attached reproducer, the rejected size is 40000×40000. A retried `seek(1)` followed by `load()` then reaches `load_prepare()`, which calls `Image.core.fill()` with that size to decode a single pixel. Peak memory rises from 17 MiB to 1700 MiB before a 3 GiB address-space cap stops the next allocation. `Image.new("RGB", im.size, ...)` and `rotate(..., expand=True)` also allocate from the stale size.

The default paths are unaffected: plain `Image.open()` plus `load()`, `ImageSequence.Iterator`, and `n_frames`/`is_animated`. The ordering was introduced in c9f1b35e9810 ("Added GIF decompression bomb check", 2022-06-30, first released in 9.2.0), the check added for CVE-2022-45198. The two dispose-extent checks later in the same function already validate before using the size, and the attached patch makes this check follow the same order.

## Details

`GifImageFile._seek()` lets a later frame enlarge the image, and performs the
decompression-bomb check for the new size only *after* storing it on the object:

```python

x0, y0 = i16(s, 0), i16(s, 2)
x1, y1 = x0 + i16(s, 4), y0 + i16(s, 6)
if (x1 > self.size[0] or y1 > self.size[1]) and update_image:
    self._size = max(x1, self.size[0]), max(y1, self.size[1])   # state mutated
    Image._decompression_bomb_check(self._size)                 # ...then validated
```

`_decompression_bomb_check()` (`src/PIL/Image.py:3586`) raises
`DecompressionBombError` for anything above `2 * MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`
(178 956 970 px by default), but by then `self._size` already holds the rejected
value and nothing restores it: `seek()` (`GifImagePlugin.py:166-179`) only rolls
back on `EOFError`, and `_seek(0)` only ever grows `_size`. The object that the
application still holds therefore reports `im.size == (40000, 40000)` while
`im.im` is the 1×1 buffer of frame 0. Compare the two dispose-extent checks a
few lines further down in the same function (`GifImagePlugin.py:383` and `:407`),
which call `_decompression_bomb_check(dispose_size)` *before* the corresponding
`Image.core.fill()`, and `TiffImagePlugin.load_prepare()`
(`src/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py:1319-1321`), which checks `_tile_size` before
allocating from it.

With this 60-byte GIF (hex)

```
47494638396101000100800000000000ffffff          GIF89a, 1x1 screen, 2-entry global palette
2c000000000100010000 02 024401 00               frame 0: 1x1 @ (0,0), LZW data
2c00000000409c409c00

When an application opens an untrusted Encapsulated PostScript file and asks Pillow to render it at a larger scale, Pillow has Ghostscript produce an image several times bigger than Pillow's configured size limit allows. The size check runs only after Ghostscript has finished rendering and written the full raw image to a temporary file. An attacker who can upload a file of about 100 bytes makes each such request spend scale² times the Ghostscript rendering work and temporary disk space that the limit is meant to permit. For example, at scale 2 that is a 972 MB temporary file.

The cause is in `Ghostscript()` in `src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py`. It multiplies the file-declared size by the caller's `scale` (lines 93-94) and passes the product to `gs` as the `-g` output geometry. It never calls `Image._decompression_bomb_check()` on the scaled size. The only check is the one `Image.open()` ran on the unscaled size, so a file declaring 9000×9000 passes, and `load(scale=2)` then asks Ghostscript for 18000×18000 (3.6× `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS`). * The multiplier is an integer chosen by the application, not by the file.
* With the default warning filter, `Image.open()` already lets files up to 2× the limit reach Ghostscript at `scale=1`.
* Any application feeding untrusted files to Ghostscript is already exposed to a tiny file that keeps Ghostscript busy indefinitely, since `gs` runs with no timeout.

Pillow hands back leftover process memory as image pixels when it opens a small crafted TIFF file. ## Summary

A small attacker-supplied TIFF can be opened and loaded normally, then reach an out-of-bounds read when an application saves it back to TIFF with retained metadata. The fixed reproducer is a 1×1, 16-bit grayscale, PackBits-compressed TIFF containing tag 320 (ColorMap) with **768 SHORT values**: three zero-filled planes of 256 entries each. No Python object is forged and no metadata is injected after loading.

Pillow's TIFF encoder allocates **768 × 2 = 1536 bytes**, then passes three plane pointers separated by 256 SHORT entries to libtiff. With `BitsPerSample = 16`, libtiff instead expects **65536 SHORT values per plane** and attempts a **131072-byte read** from a plane pointer. Existing ASAN observations identify a heap-buffer-overflow READ crossing the 1536-byte allocation made in `PyImaging_LibTiffEncoderNew`.

The malformed ColorMap need not be a valid palette for this grayscale image. The issue is that accepted metadata is forwarded on save without reconciling the fixed plane extent with the effective sample depth. Opening/loading alone is not the demonstrated fault; the encoder path is required.

items.title: Pillow: Unbounded recursion parsing a PDF page tree or trailer chain (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-42310)
items.summary:
### Summary
When an application appends to an existing PDF with `Image.save(..., format="PDF", append=True)`, Pillow parses that file with `PdfParser`. Two recursive parsers have no effective bound. `linearize_page_tree` follows `/Kids` with no visited set or depth limit, so a cyclic or duplicated page tree recurses without end. `read_prev_trailer` rejects only an exactly repeated `/Prev` offset, so a long chain of unique offsets still recurses. The trailer-loop guard added for CVE-2026-42310 does not cover either case.

### Details
`linearize_page_tree` recurses on `/Kids` with no cycle or depth check:

- `src/PIL/PdfParser.py:1078-1092`

`read_prev_trailer` catches only a repeated offset:

- `src/PIL/PdfParser.py:697-720` (the `processed_offsets` check at `:714-718` is the CVE-2026-42310 fix; a unique-offset chain slips past it)

### PoC
```python
from PIL import PdfParser

# A page tree whose /Pages nodes reference each other in a cycle (2 -> 3 -> 2).
objs = {
    1: b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
    2: b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
    3: b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [2 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
}
buf = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.4\n")
off = {}
for oid in (1, 2, 3):
    off[oid] = len(buf)
    buf += b"%d 0 obj\n" % oid + objs[oid] + b"\nendobj\n"
xref = len(buf)
buf += b"xref\n0 4\n0000000000 65535 f \n"
buf += b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % off[o] for o in (1, 2, 3))
buf += b"trailer\n<< /Root 1 0 R /Size 4 >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % xref
open("poc.pdf", "wb").write(buf)

PdfParser.PdfParser("poc.pdf", mode="r+b")   # append=True parses the existing file the same way
```

Run it:
```
$ python 11_poc.py
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

The 315-byte file triggers the recursion on parse. A duplicated (non-cyclic) `/Kids` tree instead produces super-linear CPU and memory work, and a long unique-offset `/Prev` chain triggers the trailer-side recursion.

### Impact
A service that appends to user-supplied PDFs, for example a stamping or watermarking pipeline, can be driven into uncaught recursion or heavy CPU and memory use before any image is written. Follow-up to CVE-2026-42310. Since Pillow's policy discourages filing plain Python exceptions as denial of service, lead with the cyclic-tree case, which burns CPU and memory rather than only raising `RecursionError`. The fix is a visited set plus a depth limit in both parsers.

items.title: Pillow tiled-TIFF decoder reads past tile buffer in copy4 (Unpack.c:1290)
Pillow: OOB read in TiffDecode.c tile and RGBA paths leaks heap memory into pixels
items.summary:
```
============================================================================
OOB read in TiffDecode.c tile and RGBA paths leaks heap memory into pixels
Location: src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c:483  in _decodeTile()
Commit:   a707c6b21c313880d0771e54965d142dd42358b6
============================================================================
```

Pillow reads past the end of a heap buffer when decoding certain malformed compressed TIFF files, and copies the bytes it reads into the pixels of the image it returns. An attacker who can get an application to open and load an image file, for example by uploading it to a service that returns thumbnails, previews or converted images, gets back fragments of that process's heap memory, including pointer values. A slightly larger file instead crashes the process. No special settings are needed, and nothing is written out of bounds.

The bug is in `_decodeTile()` and `_decodeAsRGBA()` in `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c`. Both size their decode buffer from libtiff's view of the pixel layout (`TIFFTileSize()`/`TIFFTileRowSize()`, or `img.width * 4`). They then unpack each row with the unpacker that `TiffImagePlugin._setup()` chose from Pillow's own parse of the directory, and neither checks that the unpacker's input row fits inside the row libtiff produced. `_decodeStrip()` has exactly this check, added for OSS-Fuzz `crash-0da0` in 8.2.0, but the tile and RGBA paths never got it.

The two parsers can be made to disagree with a duplicated `PhotometricInterpretation` or `BitsPerSample` tag, because libtiff keeps the first occurrence and Pillow keeps the last. Pillow then unpacks 4 to 8 bytes per pixel from rows that libtiff filled with 1 to 4 bytes, so the last rows of each tile are read from beyond the buffer. The disclosed memory is a few tile rows past the buffer, and the attacker chooses the tile width. The amount does not grow with the number of tiles, because the buffer is reused for every tile.

The tile half was introduced in 1c295bf43 (first released in 8.2.0). The RGBA half was introduced in eb8c1206d, the CVE-2020-35654 fix (8.1.0).

The attached reproducer runs against an unmodified build. It writes three roughly 400-byte files that load without error, yet the last pixel rows of each change with glibc's malloc fill pattern and contain heap pointer bytes. A fourth file with a 65536x16 tile segfaults in `copy4` ← `_decodeTile` (`TiffDecode.c:483`) in most runs, depending on what is mapped after the buffer.

## Details

`_decodeTile()` and `_decodeAsRGBA()` in `src/libImaging/TiffDecode.c` size `state->buffer` from what libtiff says it will produce (`TIFFTileSize()`, resp. `img.width * 4`), but unpack each row with the shuffler that `TiffImagePlugin._setup()` selected from Pillow's *own* parse of the IFD. Nothing in either function checks that the unpacker's input row (`width * state->bits / 8` bytes) fits inside the row libtiff wrote. `_decodeStrip()` has exactly that check; the other two do not. Whenever the two IFD parsers disagree about the pixel layout — a tag with the wrong count or type that libtiff ignores but Pillow accepts, or a duplicated `PhotometricInterpretation`/`BitsPerSample`/`SamplesPerPixel` entry (libtiff keeps the first occurrence, `ImageFileDirectory_v2.load()` the last) — the unpacker reads past the end of the heap buffer and the bytes it reads become pixels of the returned image. Any Pillow rawmode wider than libtiff's actual sample layout works (`RGBX`, `RGB;16N`, `RGBA;16N`, `I;32`, `F;32F`, …); `RGBA;16N` (64 bits/pixel) against 1-bit libtiff data is the largest ratio, where every row after the first of each tile is read almost entirely from beyond the buffer.

The ~400-byte TIFF `tile_count2.tif` generated by the reproducer — one 16x16 tile, `BitsPerSample 8`, `SamplesPerPixel 1`, `Compression 8` (Adobe Deflate), and `PhotometricInterpretation` written as a SHORT with **count 2** (`6, 6`) — is opened by `Image.open()` as mode `RGB` with libtiff rawmode `RGBX`

@angular/common: XSRF Token Leakage via URL Parsing Discrepancy in Angular HTTP Client (Incomplete fix for CVE-2025-66035)
items.summary:
An incomplete fix for [GHSA-58c5-g7wp-6w37](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-58c5-g7wp-6w37) (`CVE-2025-66035`) in `@angular/common`'s HTTP Client (`HttpClient`) allows Cross-Site Request Forgery (XSRF) tokens to be leaked to attacker-controlled cross-origin domains when requests use URLs that exploit parsing discrepancies between regular expressions and the browser's WHATWG URL parser.

### Technical Description

To address `CVE-2025-66035`, `xsrfInterceptorFn` introduced a regular expression (`const ABSOLUTE_URL_REGEX = /^(?:https?:)?\/\//i`) to detect and skip absolute and protocol-relative URLs before attaching the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header.

However, browsers resolve request URLs passed to `fetch()` and `XMLHttpRequest.open()` using the **WHATWG URL parser**. For `http:` and `https:` schemes, the WHATWG URL standard performs several normalizations prior to resolving the authority/origin:
* Backslashes (`\`) are treated as forward slashes (`/`) — e.g., `/\evil.example/x`, `\\evil.example/x`, `\/evil.example/x`, `https:\\evil.example/x`, `https:/\evil.example/x`.
* Leading and trailing C0 control characters and spaces (`<= 0x20`) are stripped — e.g., `' //evil.example/x'`, `'\0//evil.example/x'`, `'\x1f//evil.example/x'`.
* ASCII tab (`\t`), newline (`\n`), and carriage return (`\r`) characters are removed anywhere in the input — e.g., `'/\t/evil.example/x'`, `'/\n/evil.example/x'`, `'htt\tps://evil.example/x'`.

Because these URLs do not match `/^(?:https?:)?\/\//i`, `xsrfInterceptorFn` treats them as relative same-origin URLs and attaches the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header, while the browser resolves and dispatches the request to the cross-origin host (`evil.example`).

Note: Angular `21.0.3+` and `22.x` replaced the regular expression with a WHATWG `new URL(req.url, locationOrigin)` origin comparison in [#65683](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/65683) and were already unaffected. However, the `20.3.x` LTS branch retained the regular expression until `20.3.34`.

### Impact

The token leakage bypasses Angular's built-in XSRF protection on affected versions, allowing an attacker to capture the user's valid `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header if their server permits the request and custom header via CORS. Once obtained, the attacker can perform Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks against the victim user's session.

### Attack Preconditions

1. The victim's Angular application must have **XSRF protection enabled** (enabled by default in `HttpClient`).
2. The attacker must be able to make the application send a state-changing HTTP request (e.g., `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`) to a URL they control (such as `/\attacker.example/api` or ` //attacker.example/api`).

### Patches

The issue is resolved by parsing and comparing the request URL's origin against the application's current origin using the standard `URL` constructor (`new URL(req.url, locationOrigin)`).

* `21.0.3` (and all `22.x` releases)
* `20.3.34`

### Workarounds

If you cannot immediately upgrade to a patched version:
* Validate and normalize outgoing request URLs using `new URL(url, window.location.origin)` and verify that `parsedUrl.origin === window.location.origin` before passing dynamic URLs to mutating `HttpClient` requests.
* Avoid passing untrusted or user-controlled URLs to `HttpClient` mutating methods.

MCP  TypeScript server SDK: Shared transport or server instances delivered one HTTP client's messages to another
items.summary:
### Summary
In affected versions, an MCP server reached over HTTP could deliver one client's responses and notifications to another client. This happened when clients shared one stateless transport, or one `McpServer` or `Server` instance.

Messages were matched to a connection by JSON-RPC `id` alone. SDK clients number requests from 0, so ids collide in normal use.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if more than one client can reach your HTTP endpoint and your code creates the transport or the server once at startup, instead of once per request or per session. Until this release, the README examples of `@modelcontextprotocol/hono`, `express`, `fastify` and `node` showed that pattern.

Affected versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0.

Not affected:

- `createMcpHandler()` with a factory that builds a new server on every call
- stdio servers
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.26.0 and later

### Fix
Upgrade to `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.0 or later.

**You also need to change your code.** The SDK now refuses to be shared, so an affected app fails requests after upgrading: a second `connect()` rejects with `ALREADY_CONNECTED`, and a stateless transport rejects its second request.

Change to one of these:

- **`createMcpHandler()`:** pass a factory that builds a new `McpServer` on every call.
- **Per request:** build a new `McpServer` and a new transport inside the request handler.
- **Per session:** set `sessionIdGenerator` and keep one `McpServer` and one transport per session.

If you cannot upgrade yet, the same change fixes affected versions.

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK: One HTTP request within the default size limit could exhaust server memory during validation
items.summary:
### Summary
In affected versions, servers put no limit on how many array elements and object keys they validated in one request. One HTTP request within the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust the server's memory, and the process aborted with `JavaScript heap out of memory`.

No credentials are needed, unless you authenticate requests before they reach the SDK.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if clients you do not fully trust can reach your server over HTTP. The risk is highest for `McpServer` tools whose input contains an array or a record. stdio-only servers are not affected.

Affected versions:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.3.0 through 1.31.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0

### Fix
Upgrade to:

- 1.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later
- 2.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.0 or later

**Upgrading alone changes nothing.** The patched versions add an `McpServer` option, `maxToolInputElements`, that is off by default. Make both of these changes:

1. Set `maxToolInputElements` just above the largest input your tools need, for example `new McpServer(info, { maxToolInputElements: 10_000 })`. It counts array elements and object keys in a call's arguments. A call over the limit gets an `isError: true` result.
2. Lower the request size limit to what your tools need. The option covers tool arguments only, and the size limit covers everything else. Set `maxRequestBodySize` on the transport or `createMcpHandler()`. If you parse the body yourself, for example with `express.json()` or Fastify, set that parser's limit.

If you cannot upgrade yet, make the second change. `maxRequestBodySize` needs `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.1 or `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.1.0. Below that, use a reverse proxy.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Absolute-form request targets can spoof Request.scheme
items.summary:
### Summary

An attacker sending an absolute-form request can spoof the scheme used.

### Impact

If user code depends on the `Request.scheme` attribute for anything security related, an attacker may be able to circumvent this logic, tricking the application into thinking a connection is encrypted when it is not, or vice versa.

### Workaround

A WAF rule to reject absolute-form requests (legitimate requests should only use this form for proxies).

items.title: AIOHTTP: Cookie from subdomain can remove Host-Only Scope from existing cookies
items.summary:
### Summary

A subdomain can remove the Host-Only flag from an existing cookie to a parent domain.

### Impact

A user accessing untrusted subdomains could see their Host-Only protections stripped from cookies. Given most usecases won't reflect these cookies to a browser, the impact is limited.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Connector pool exhaustion via Max-Age overflow
items.summary:
### Summary

An overflow in Max-Age processing can skip closing a connection.

### Impact

An attacker may be able to exhaust the connection pool temporarily, until garbage collection resolves the connections.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request smuggling
items.summary:
### Summary

The pure Python parser is vulnerable to an HTTP request smuggling attack.

### Impact

If users are using the Python parser (`AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS`, or not a standard wheel installed), then an application may be vulnerable to a request smuggling attack.

### Workaround

Switch to the default C parser.

items.title: AIOHTTP: File descriptor exhaustion in multipart requests
items.summary:
### Summary

An attacker can exhaust file descriptors with specially crafted multipart requests.

### Impact

If a handler uses `Request.post()`, it may be possible for an attacker to use an unlimited number of file descriptors, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion.

items.title: launch-editor: Editor CLI flag misinterpretation causing arbitrary command execution for some editors
items.summary:
### Summary

`launch-editor` forwarded file paths directly to editors without sanitization. If a path resembles a CLI flag, editors like Vim may interpret it as a command, potentially causing unintended file overwrites or command execution.

### Impact

#### Direct `launch-editor` users

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- The first argument of `launchEditor` can start with `+` or `-` or the user is using WSL

#### `launch-editor-middleware` users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- launch-editor older than v2.2.0 is used, or the user is using WSL

#### Vite users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
  - Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)
- The user is using WSL

### Details

`launchEditor(file)` function passes the file name as-is to the editor if the file with that file name exists. If the file name starts with `-` (also `+` for Vim), the editor treats them as flags rather than positional arguments. For example, Vim treats arguments starting with `+` as an Ex command. As a result, an existing relative directory such as:
```
+call writefile(["SAFE_MARKER"],"LAUNCH_EDITOR_MARKER")|qa!
```
is not treated as a filename when passed to Vim. Vim executes the embedded Ex command.

The following editor has a potentially destructive operation exposed to the CLI arguments:
- Vim (including gVim)
- MacVim
- Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via plugin messages)

`launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ converts the passed file path to an absolute path so those are not affected as long as the user is not using WSL. For WSL, `launch-editor` converts the paths to relative paths internally, so those are still affected.

Vite 2.0.0+ uses `launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ so the WSL users are only affected.

items.title: launch-editor: `fs.existsSync()` existence check can be bypassed on Windows
items.summary:
### Summary

`launch-editor` checked `fs.existsSync(fileName)` before passing a supplied path to an editor command. On Windows, an attacker can bypass this check with a crafted path ending in `\\..:line:column`. This removes the requirement that the attacker be able to place a file with a malicious filename.

Combined with the `%` escaping issue described in [GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv), this bypass can lead to OS command injection when an attacker controls the file argument.

### Impact

Only apps that runs on Windows is affected.

### Details

The earlier advisory assumed that `fs.existsSync()` required an attacker-controlled filename to exist. This advisory covers a bypass of that requirement.

A crafted value ending in `\\..:1:1` is interpreted differently by `launch-editor-middleware`, `launch-editor`, and Windows:

1. `launch-editor-middleware` calls `path.resolve()` while the final path component is `..:1:1`, so it is not treated as a parent-directory component.
2. `launch-editor` treats `:1:1` as a line-and-column suffix and removes it, leaving a path ending in `\\..`.
3. On Windows, `fs.existsSync()` accepts the resulting path as the existing parent directory even though the attacker-controlled preceding component does not exist.
4. Because the existence check passes, the crafted filename reaches the Windows shell command.

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK: Server bearer authentication accepted tokens issued for another service
items.summary:
### Summary
In affected versions, the SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check that a token was issued for your server (its audience). Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if your HTTP server uses `requireBearerAuth()` or `verifyBearerToken()`, its authorization server also issues tokens for other services, and your `verifyAccessToken()` does not check the token's audience (`aud`) itself.

Affected versions:

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.6.0 through 1.31.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0
- `@modelcontextprotocol/express` 2.0.0 through 2.0.1
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy` 2.0.0 through 2.3.0

### Fix
Upgrade to:

- 1.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.0 or later
- 2.x: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.0 or later, together with `@modelcontextprotocol/express` 2.0.2 or later if you use it
- `@modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy` 2.3.1 or later

**Upgrading alone changes nothing.** The patched versions add an `expectedResource` setting that is off by default. To turn the check on, make both of these changes together:

1. Pass the audience your authorization server puts in tokens for your server: `requireBearerAuth({ verifier, expectedResource: new URL('https://mcp.example.com/mcp') })`.
2. Return the token's audience from `verifyAccessToken()` as `AuthInfo.resource`, also a `URL`.

A token for another service then gets `401`. With only the first change, every request gets `401`.

If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose `aud` does not include your server inside `verifyAccessToken()`. That closes the issue on every version.

items.title: uv's bundled CA store trusts an emSign root whose intermediate CA keys are compromised
items.summary:
By default, uv verifies TLS connections against a vendored copy of the `webpki-root-certs` bundle. Versions before 0.13.4 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to that root have compromised private keys, and the CA has revoked them.

An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

uv 0.13.4 removes the root from its vendored bundle, following `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.10. Upgrade to 0.13.4 or later.

items.title: certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys
items.summary:
Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them. 

An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname. If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer.

Certifi 2026.10.18 removed all emSign roots from the bundle. Certifi 2026.10.19 restored the emSign roots that are not affected. Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.
